title: Chemical potentials from structure factors: II. Charged multi-component mixtures
authors: Xiaoyu Wang, Roya Savoj, Musahid Ahmed, Bingqing Cheng
abstract: The chemical potentials of charged multi-component mixtures are central to electrolyte thermo- dynamics, but remain difficult to compute from atomistic simulations. The S0 method enables computing chemical potentials of mixtures from equilibrium molecular dynamics simulations. Here we extend the S0 method to charged mixtures by combining the composition-space framework developed in Part I: Neutral Multi-component Mixtures with a Coulombic treatment of the small- wavenumber limits of static structure factors. This approach separates thermodynamically relevant neutral composition fluctuations from forbidden macroscopic charge fluctuations, and further ac- counts for charge-neutrality constraints. We use the method to compute the chemical potentials of multiple-halide aqueous salt solutions, elucidating the ion-specific thermodynamic effects. We also calculate the mixing free energies of molten salt mixtures, demonstrating the importance of correctly describing long-wavelength electrostatic correlations.
summary: This paper develops an advanced theoretical method to compute chemical potentials in charged multi-component mixtures by modifying the standard structure factor analysis to correctly handle long-range Coulomb interactions. By separating charge fluctuations, the authors achieve consistent calculations for aqueous and molten salt systems, revealing ion-specific thermodynamic effects and structural reorganization mechanisms.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is the accurate computation of chemical potentials in complex, charged multi-component mixtures, which is crucial for understanding electrolyte thermodynamics but difficult using standard atomistic simulation techniques.
main_result: The authors successfully extend the S0 method by incorporating a Coulombic treatment into the structure factor analysis, leading to consistent calculations of excess chemical potentials for aqueous and molten salt systems.
method: The method combines a composition-space framework with a specialized treatment of the small-wavenumber limit of the static structure factor matrix, $	ext{SBC}(k)$, to correctly account for long-range electrostatic correlations and charge neutrality.
model_or_system: The work models charged multi-component systems, specifically focusing on aqueous salt solutions (e.g., $	ext{NaCl}/	ext{NaX}$) and molten salt mixtures (e.g., $	ext{MgCl}_2-	ext{NaCl}$). The theory is applied to calculate thermodynamic properties like chemical potentials and mixing free energies.
key_observables: Chemical potentials ($\mu_\alpha$), partial static structure factors ($S_{\alpha eta}(k)$), and the charge-density structure factor ($S_{ZZ}(k)$).
important_parameters: Small wavevector limit ($k 	o 0$), ionic strength, and the specific composition of the salt mixture.
main_assumptions: The theory assumes that the thermodynamically relevant neutral composition fluctuations can be separated from the forbidden macroscopic charge fluctuations, and that the structure factor matrix has a finite limit at zero wavevector.
figures_summary: Figures compare simulated partial structure factors using different fitting methods (bare-Coulomb vs. OZ) and show the calculated excess chemical potentials ($\mu_{	ext{ex}}$) for various salt mixtures, demonstrating anion-specific effects.
paper_structure: The paper builds upon previous work (Part I) by extending the S0 method to charged systems. It details the theoretical framework involving the partial structure-factor matrix $	ext{SBC}(k)$, applies this to aqueous electrolytes to calculate $\mu_{	ext{ex}}$, and then extends the methodology to analyze structural reorganization and mixing thermodynamics in molten salts.
why_interesting: While focused on classical statistical mechanics, the rigorous treatment of long-range Coulomb interactions and the development of a specialized structure factor matrix $	ext{SBC}(k)$ for charged systems represents a sophisticated theoretical extension of many-body correlation functions, which has parallels in quantum field theory approaches to interacting quantum systems.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: Fitting partial structure factors for aqueous NaCl at 𝑥Na = 𝑥Cl = 0.02. Panels (a–f) compare simulated partial structure factor components with the bare-Coulomb fit, the independent scalar Ornstein–Zernike fit, and the full Ornstein–Zernike matrix fit. Panel (g) shows the corresponding charge–charge structure factor 𝑆𝑍𝑍(𝑘), and the reference scaling curve 𝑘2/𝜅2 𝐷.
FIG. 2: Excess chemical potential for NaCl salt in water, 𝜇ex NaCl(𝑥), obtained by integrating chemical-potential derivatives inferred from fitted S0

FIG. 3: Excess chemical potentials for mixed aqueous salts, derived from the bare-Coulomb matrix fit. Panels (a–d) show Gaussian process-integrated surfaces of the neutral ion-pair excess chemical potentials: 𝜇ex NaCl and 𝜇ex NaI for NaCl/NaI in water, and 𝜇ex NaCl and 𝜇ex NaF for NaCl/NaF in water. Panels (e–h) show one-dimensional slices through the same surfaces; line colors indicate fixed 𝑥I (e), fixed 𝑥F (g), or fixed 𝑥Cl (f, h), as marked by the inset color bars. Shaded bands show standard error, and the dashed gray curve shows the reference values from NaCl-water simulations.

FIG. 4: Local and long-range structure of molten NaCl at 1200 K and 1 bar. a Radial distribution functions, 𝑔(𝑟), for Na–Na, Na–Cl and Cl–Cl, computed using MACELES (solid lines) and MACE-SR (dotted lines) models. Error bars denote standard errors from a time-block analysis. b Corresponding charge–charge structure factors, 𝑆ZZ(𝑘), for MACELES (blue squares) and MACE-SR (red circles). The reference curve 𝑘2/𝜅2 D is drawn with the Debye wavevector 𝜅D = 5.37 ˚A −1.

FIG. 5: Partial structure factors for molten NaCl at 1200 K and 1 bar. a–c: MACELES MD results for the Na–Na, Na–Cl and Cl–Cl components, shown with the bare-Coulomb matrix fit (solid lines) and the full Ornstein–Zernike matrix fit (dotted lines). Fits were performed over 𝑘2 < 𝑘2 cut = 0.01 × 4𝜋2/˚𝐴2, indicated by the vertical dotted lines. Error bars denote standard errors from a block analysis. d: Corresponding charge–charge structure factor 𝑆ZZ(𝑘). The dot-dashed line shows the Stillinger–Lovett limiting form 𝑘2/𝜅2 D, using the fitted inverse Debye screening length 𝜅D = 5.00 ˚A −1.
